3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Vina, Estela and I sat in Palas Rezna's most ornate stateroom, awaiting the arrival of Queen Beatrice Livingston.
3.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DenounceSO"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DenounceSO"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Order_GoldenGuard_Expanded"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Order_GoldenGuard_Expanded"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Order_RizianForeignIntelligence_Expanded"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Order_RizianForeignIntelligence_Expanded"] == true) == false)

4.speaker: Pabel Adria
4.text: "Announcing Her Excellency Beatrice Livingston, Queen of the Four Corners of Merkopa, Defender of Castle Tzarsbough, Conqueror of the Tranquil Sea, Stout Protector of the Ancient Lands of Rum, Descendant of the Most Honorable King Edward the First and the Ruler of Rumburg.”

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Pabel came in through the stateroom door. He took a deep breath.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: He stepped aside and Queen Beatrice entered. She was wearing an emerald-green gown that matched her tiara.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Vina, Estela and I rose to greet the queen.

12.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
12.text: "What a pleasure it is to see you, Your Majesty. We barely had the chance to speak at the coronation."

15.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
15.text: "Why, you're looking more and more like your mother every day. I hope your father's proud of the lady you've become."

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: Beatrice embraced her tightly before moving on to my mother.

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: She tilted her face upwards and gave a short sniff.

20.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
20.text: "The palace looks as magnificent as always, but I fear a chat with your housekeeper may be in order. Every time I visit, it smells just the faintest bit like trash."

21.speaker: Estela Toras
21.text: "Funny, I do seem to detect an unpleasant draft of hot air. But only since you walked in."

22.speaker: Player_Romus
22.text: "Let's be civil, ladies. We have important state issues to discuss."

24.speaker: Player_Romus
24.text: "Pabel, please look into these matters at once. The air quality in the palace may be compromised."

27.speaker: Estela Toras
27.text: "Then I shall take my leave. I have a terribly urgent appointment on the other side of the palace."

28.speaker: Estela Toras
28.text: "If you'll excuse me, I shall take my leave. I have a terribly urgent appointment on the other side of the palace."

29.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
29.text: "By all means, Your Highness. Our chatter is far more boring than the sort of carousing you're used to."

30.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
30.text: "Vina, why don't you run along as well? We'll catch up over supper."

32.speaker: Vina Toras
32.text: "Sure, Aunt Bea. Have the staff give my room a ring when you're done."

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: He filled two porcelain cups for us, then escorted Vina and my mother out the door.

34.speaker: Player_Romus
34.text: "Queen Mother Estela may have a common upbringing, but she's part of the royal family. Please respect her as such."

37.speaker: Player_Romus
37.text: "To what do we owe this pleasure, Your Excellency?"

40.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
40.text: "Splendid. King Consort Boris sends his sincerest regrets. He had to oversee some air force exercises."

41.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
41.text: "Of course we are the same age, Your Majesty, but I've worn my crown for many years longer than you have yours."

42.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
42.text: "And I and my country are far more experienced at dealing with the Republic of Wehlen and their backers in the CSP."

46.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
46.text: "Sending your own investigators to ferret out the bombing culprit is a good start. It shows President Smolak you are unwilling to play by his terms."

50.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
50.text: "By indicating that you regard your own countrymen as culpable for the bombing, you are putting yourself in a position of weakness from the start."

51.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
51.text: "By apologizing to President Smolak for a perfectly justified speech, you are putting yourself in a position of weakness from the start."
51.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Order_RizianForeignIntelligence_Expanded"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DenounceSO"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == true)

52.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
52.text: "But how do you plan to follow that up? What will you do if Mr. Smolak fails to relinquish his hold on Zille?"

53.speaker: Player_Romus
53.text: "That won't happen. President Smolak will respect the rule of law."

54.speaker: Player_Romus
54.text: "If it comes down to it, I'm prepared to fight."

55.speaker: Player_Romus
55.text: "We will exercise diplomacy until an agreement is reached."

56.speaker: Player_Romus
56.text: "I know Rumburg has its own agenda when it comes to Wehlen. Rizia's path will be different."

57.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
57.text: "Our only agenda is neutralizing the threat that this unpredictable regime poses to its neighbors. Including you."

59.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
59.text: "To that end, Rumburg is prepared to provide assistance with the delicate situation in which you've found yourself."

60.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
60.text: "That sounds simply wonderful, Your Majesty. Until you arrive at the bargaining table and realize your pockets are empty."

61.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
61.text: "Have you thought about your next steps? What will you do if Mr. Smolak fails to relinquish his hold on Zille?"

68.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
68.text: "You denied that your countrymen were culpable for the attack. But you must realize President Smolak will not take your words at face value."
68.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Order_RizianForeignIntelligence_Expanded"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DenounceSO"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true)

69.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
69.text: "You have expressed no opinion on the incident thus far. You must realize that President Smolak will see that as an admission of guilt."
69.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Order_RizianForeignIntelligence_Expanded"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DenounceSO"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleBombApology"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn03_ZilleIncidentResponse_DefendSO"] == true) == false)

73.speaker: Player_Romus
73.text: "I'm already funding a Rizian cultural organization in Zille. That should get locals on my side."

74.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
74.text: "A good monarch must anticipate every eventuality. No matter how unlikely he or she believes it is."

76.speaker: Narrator
76.text: Beatrice leaned forward and held my gaze.

77.speaker: Player_Romus
77.text: "I thought this was a family visit, Your Excellency. Can we save the politics for another time?"

78.speaker: Player_Romus
78.text: "You've helped us so much over the years. I would not ask more of you."

84.speaker: Narrator
84.text: She shot me a piercing glance. I wondered how much Lena had told her.

85.speaker: Narrator
85.text: She looked at me with what seemed like genuine compassion.

87.speaker: Pabel Adria
87.text: "I'll see you two out. Just a moment."

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: Pabel walked Beatrice and myself over to a pair of velvet armchairs. Next to them was a table upon which a towering silver Rumburgian tea urn had been set up.

89.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
89.text: "How are the princess' marriage plans coming along?"

91.speaker: Player_Romus
91.text: "I wouldn't know. I told her I won't be arranging her marriage."

92.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
92.text: "Heavens, no. My Bradley is still betrothed to the Duchess of Thompsfort."

93.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
93.text: "Much as I'd like to continue our tradition of royal intermarriage, this pairing is necessary to secure northwestern Rumburg's continued loyalty. Surely you understand."

94.speaker: Player_Romus
94.text: "A shame. They would have made beautiful children."

96.speaker: Player_Romus
96.text: "I was joking. They're cousins, for Dast's sake."

97.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
97.text: "That never stopped any of our noble ancestors."

98.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
98.text: "We royals are an endangered breed, you know. We've got to tend to our lineages as we would a rose garden."

99.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
99.text: "I'm sure you'll find just as suitable a match for my brilliant niece."

100.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
100.text: "Indeed they would have. But you'll find another suitable a match for my brilliant niece, I'm sure."

104.speaker: Player_Romus
104.text: "It doesn't matter, anyway. I already told her she can marry whomever she wants."

109.speaker: Player_Romus
109.text: "I'm on the lookout for candidates. Someone from one of our other royal houses, perhaps."

113.speaker: Player_Romus
113.text: "You'll have to ask her yourself. We're not on the best terms these days."

114.speaker: Player_Romus
114.text: "Honestly, I have too much on my mind to even start to think about that."

115.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
115.text: "Very good. As you'll recall, I promised my Bradley to the Duchess of Thompsfort to secure the loyalty of our country's northwestern regions."

116.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
116.text: "We royals are an endangered breed, you know. We've got to tend to our lineages as we would a rose garden."

118.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
118.text: "I lost my father at only 16, as you know. There were so many times over the years that I wished for his guidance."

119.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
119.text: "Well, don't dilly-dally much longer. An unmarried royal is catnip for the tabloids."

120.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
120.text: "They had quite the field day with my Bradley before I secured his betrothal."

121.speaker: Player_Romus
121.text: "If that means inbreeding, perhaps it's best to let the garden die."

122.speaker: Player_Romus
122.text: "I agree. But first cousins are too closely related for my comfort."

123.speaker: Player_Romus
123.text: "I don't see the harm in allowing a few exotic plants to blossom here and there."

124.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
124.text: "Choose the wrong ones, and the weeds will spread faster than you can pull them out."

125.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
125.text: "Better a cousin than a commoner, no?"

126.speaker: Player_Romus
126.text: "Fear not. The garden of House Toras shall remain in bloom for a long, long time."

127.speaker: Player_Romus
127.text: "If that means forcing my daughter into an unhappy union, perhaps it's best to let the garden die."

128.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
128.text: "We royals are an endangered breed, you know. We've got to tend to our lineages as we would a rose garden."

129.speaker: Player_Romus
129.text: "Precisely my thinking. It's good to speak with someone who understands these things."

131.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
131.text: "You're lucky to have such a relationship in your life. Cherish it."

132.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
132.text: "With the help of House Livingston, it shall bloom on only the richest of soil."

133.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
133.text: "If the garden dies, your ties to House Livingston die with it."

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: An informal supper with my sister-in-law was scheduled for the evening. But for now, the protocol for an official diplomatic visit had to be observed.

138.speaker: Player_Romus
138.text: "She's as stubborn as her mother was, that's for sure."

142.speaker: Player_Romus
142.text: "I wouldn't call her a 'lady''. She's been neglecting her duties as princess."

143.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
143.text: "Oh, my. So young, and already preparing for the crown."

144.speaker: Vina Toras
144.text: "You were younger than me when you got yours, weren't you?"

145.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
145.text: "Good girl. It's your royal obligation to give your father hell."

147.speaker: Vina Toras
147.text: "It's lovely to see you, Aunt Bea."

148.speaker: Narrator
148.text: Queen Beatrice gave Vina a mock stern look.

149.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
149.text: "It's your royal duty to give your father hell. And it seems you're performing it admirably."

150.speaker: Player_Romus
150.text: "I am. And I know Lena would have been, too."

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: The two women gave each other air kisses, then stood back and eyed each other.

159.speaker: Narrator
159.text: Beatrice motioned for her own attendants to wait outside. We settled into our seats.

160.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
160.text: "I find your mother ever so charming. I never believed those nasty rumors about her one bit."

161.speaker: Narrator
161.text: Queen Beatrice extended her little finger and took a sip from her own cup. She smiled approvingly.

162.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
162.text: "As you may know, Rumburg is currently a major importer of Wehzek oil."

163.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
163.text: "Our nations are bound by our shared love for my sister. Such a relationship goes beyond mere transaction."

164.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
164.text: "Should you wish for something a little less subtle, I have a suggestion."

166.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
166.text: "Of course, an immediate modernization of your Monqiz port would be required to handle the excess shipping traffic."

168.speaker: Player_Romus
168.text: "I love it. You buy less oil from Wehlen, and we'll make up the difference with natural gas and other energy sources."

169.speaker: Player_Romus
169.text: "That's a lot to demand for a plan that may not even be useful or necessary."

170.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
170.text: "I'm quite sure some of the same ships that carry out our gold trade can be retrofitted to transport natural gas in its liquified form."

172.speaker: Player_Romus
172.text: "To be honest, I'm satisfied with our countries' current trade relations. I don't want to complicate them."

173.speaker: Player_Romus
173.text: "Interesting. But how would Rizian gas even reach Rumburg from here?"

174.speaker: Player_Romus
174.text: "Would we have to replace all the oil you've been purchasing? What about only part of it?"

175.speaker: Player_Romus
175.text: "So you believe Wehlen can't find another customer?"

176.speaker: Player_Romus
176.text: "This is a serious promise. What happens if I can't keep up my end of the guarantee?"

177.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
177.text: "Rumburg would prefer to eliminate its energy dependence on Wehlen entirely."

178.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
178.text: "Believe it or not, Wiktor Smolak has managed to alienate Wehlen from most of its neighbors."

179.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
179.text: "We'll have to find a more reliable trading partner. For energy as well as other materials."

180.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
180.text: "And? What do you think of the idea?"

181.speaker: Player_Romus
181.text: "I can't promise you anything. Rizia is indeed expanding its energy horizons, but we have other potential buyers in mind."

182.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
182.text: "Thrilling. How much less oil shall we buy, then?"

183.speaker: Player_Romus
183.text: "Can you halve your imports? We will provide some from our stockpiles now and more in the future." [-2 Energy, -1 Energy Per Turn, +1 Budget Per Turn]

184.speaker: Player_Romus
184.text: "Screw it, Your Excellency. Cut off Wehlen completely." [-3 Energy, -2 Energy Per Turn, +2 Budget Per Turn]

186.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
186.text: "Very bold of you. My sister didn't marry a man who takes half measures."

187.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
187.text: "You would turn your back on family that easily?"

188.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
188.text: "Are you quite sure? Remember, bilateral relations always need maintaining."

191.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
191.text: "Even if you don't ship us gas, getting that port into tip-top shape would make our gold trade more efficient."

192.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
192.text: "If we were to significantly reduce our imports, the financial pressure -- and thus your leverage over Wehlen -- would be considerable."

193.speaker: Player_Romus
193.text: "Wait. How much oil are you importing from Wehlen?"

194.speaker: Player_Romus
194.text: "I thought you hated Wehlen. But you're buying their oil?"

195.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
195.text: "Don't look so shocked. It's a partnership of convenience."

196.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
196.text: "Enough to seriously make a dent in the country's economy were our purchase orders to diminish."

198.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
198.text: "Leverage isn't the only thing I'm offering you."

199.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
199.text: "But in fact, my advisors and I have been speaking about forging new energy partnerships."

200.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
200.text: "And as it happens, Rizia is about to come into possession of quite a bit of natural gas, correct?"

201.speaker: Player_Romus
201.text: "Yes, we've discovered a new gas field. It's very exciting."

202.speaker: Player_Romus
202.text: "We don't know yet. Our scientists are still figuring out the details."

203.speaker: Player_Romus
203.text: "At least some of it belongs to Pales."

204.speaker: Player_Romus
204.text: "Rizia has enough natural gas already. We're not looking for more."

207.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
207.text: "I was about to propose that Rumburg purchase Rizian energy in lieu of Wehzek oil."

208.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
208.text: "We enrich your country and assist you with your Wehlen problem in one fell swoop."

210.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
210.text: "My proposal, then, would be for Rumburg to purchase Rizian energy in lieu of Wehzek oil."

212.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
212.text: "My advisors and I have been speaking about forging new energy partnerships."

213.speaker: Player_Romus
213.text: "You'd deprive your own people of energy just to help Rizia?"

216.speaker: Player_Romus
216.text: "What kind of timeline are you thinking about?"

217.speaker: Player_Romus
217.text: "Generous, Your Excellency. But I can't guarantee that we'll be able to access that gas field."

218.speaker: Player_Romus
218.text: "I promise you access to the gas from that field and you'll stop purchasing oil from Wehlen. I like the sound of it."

219.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
219.text: "It doesn't have to be that one particular gas field, to be honest. We'll accept other sources."

220.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
220.text: "Grant us a small amount of energy to add to our stockpile now, and we can cut off Wehlen immediately."

222.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
222.text: "I know our partners in GRACE would surely follow suit and cut their own ties."

223.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
223.text: "But of course, we wouldn't want Rizia to make any overly rash promises. So yes, a partial embargo on our end is possible."

224.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
224.text: "We can cut off our orders of Wehzek oil immediately, as long as you grant us a small amount of energy upfront to add to our stockpile."

225.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
225.text: "We'd then give you a one-year grace period to make the transition. After which, I warn you, our needs will be quite substantial."

226.speaker: Player_Romus
226.text: "Sorry, Your Excellency. I can already tell you I'm not interested."

228.speaker: Narrator
228.text: Her teacup made a soft clink as she placed it on her saucer.

231.speaker: Narrator
231.text: Queen Beatrice extended her little finger and raised her teacup to her lips. She smiled approvingly.

232.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
232.text: "Just like home. My compliments to your butler."

233.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
233.text: "Now. How are you faring a year into your reign? I know you had quite the scare in Zille."

234.speaker: Player_Romus
234.text: "I was never scared. Rizians weren't the target, after all."

235.speaker: Player_Romus
235.text: "Yes, Mother and I were lucky to get out with our lives."

236.speaker: Player_Romus
236.text: "I'm less scared by what happened than by the ramifications of it."

237.speaker: Player_Romus
237.text: "I have good security. And everything's under control now."

238.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
238.text: "That is the correct manner of thinking."

239.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
239.text: "No Rizians were harmed at all, in fact. How curious."

242.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
242.text: "Needless to say, Rumburg has been monitoring the fallout of the incident with great concern."

244.speaker: Player_Romus
244.text: "Why? How does what happened affect you?"

245.speaker: Player_Romus
245.text: "So you came all the way to Porte Drazon to... express your concern?"

247.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
247.text: "Aside from my worries about your personal safety, I foresee a scenario where Wehlen uses this tragedy to its own gain."

248.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
248.text: "I don't need an excuse to see my extended family."

249.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
249.text: "But aside from my worries about your personal safety, I foresee a scenario where Wehlen uses this tragedy to its own gain."

250.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
250.text: "Aside from my worries about your personal safety, you mean?"

251.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
251.text: "I foresee a scenario where Wehlen uses this tragedy to its own gain."

252.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
252.text: "And Wehlen amassing more power is not in either of our interests, correct, Your Majesty?"

253.speaker: Player_Romus
253.text: "Not as long as they have our land."

254.speaker: Player_Romus
254.text: "No. We've got to be very careful not to stir the pot further."

255.speaker: Player_Romus
255.text: "If they try, they will face the consequences."

256.speaker: Player_Romus
256.text: "I only want peace with Wehlen. Our countries have a historical bond."

259.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
259.text: "You and I are royals, Romus. For us, family and politics are one and the same."

266.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
266.text: "Or would you rather talk about how your coronation speech angered our partners in GRACE?"

267.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
267.text: "Or would you rather talk about how your affairs humiliated my sister until the day she died?"

268.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
268.text: "Or would you rather talk about how your daughter is nearly 20 and still not betrothed?"

269.speaker: Player_Romus
269.text: "That's quite all right. Tell me your idea."

272.speaker: Player_Romus
272.text: "I'm so sorry. It was never my intention to be unfaithful."

277.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
277.text: "You are as crucial of a member as Rumburg, Your Majesty. Do not feign naivete."

278.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
278.text: "Just as the world's remaining monarchies pledge to enter an era of increased cooperation, you tell your entire country you intend on 'giving the people a voice'.

279.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
279.text: "What am I to make of that, Your Majesty? Or Nahrburk, or the Baronies of Soradis?"

280.speaker: Player_Romus
280.text: "Giving people a voice doesn't mean giving up monarchy. Isn't your own country governed by a parliament?"

281.speaker: Player_Romus
281.text: "I got carried away in the moment. I didn't really mean it."

282.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
282.text: "Technically, yes. But it has roughly as much power as your 'House of Delegates'."

283.speaker: Player_Romus
283.text: "You can all make of it what you will."

284.speaker: Player_Romus
284.text: "I didn't realize that GRACE was so attuned to my actions as king."

285.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
285.text: "You are the unproven ruler of one of GRACE's linchpin countries. Don't be surprised that you are under scrutiny."

289.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
289.text: "I hear your behavior as king has suggested otherwise."

290.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
290.text: "It's an odd promise to simply blurt out."

291.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
291.text: "I hardly think such a flippant answer is appropriate."

292.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
292.text: "You were lucky to escape the 1926 uprising with your head. To make such a public overture towards democracy is to tempt fate."

293.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
293.text: "Of course you are free to run your country the way you like. But without GRACE's backing, you will be at the mercy of ATO and the CSP like every other country on this continent."

294.speaker: Player_Romus
294.text: "Don't worry, Your Excellency. The Rizian monarchy is not going anywhere."

295.speaker: Player_Romus
295.text: "Thank you for warning me. I shall keep your words in mind."

296.speaker: Player_Romus
296.text: "I know what I'm getting myself into."

302.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
302.text: "Excuse my short breach of decorum, but don't bullshit me, Your Majesty."

303.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
303.text: "Lena was able to put her personal resentments aside for the sake of the bond between our kingdoms. I have tried to do the same."

304.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
304.text: "But should that bond in any way falter, I cannot promise those resentments will not color my judgement."

305.speaker: Player_Romus
305.text: "I understand what you're getting at. Let's talk about Wehlen."

307.speaker: Player_Romus
307.text: "The bond will not falter. Don't forget there's also Vina."

308.speaker: Narrator
308.text: Beatrice glared at me, then smiled insincerely.

313.speaker: Player_Romus
313.text: "You know what? Let's talk about that instead."

318.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
318.text: "But let's move on to equally important matters."

319.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
319.text: "I hope you shall do more than that."

334.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
334.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_OrElse"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_OtherCustomers"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_Amount"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_Logistics"] == true

335.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
335.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_OrElse"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_OtherCustomers"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_Amount"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_Logistics"] == true) == false

336.speaker: Player_Romus
336.text: "Okay. I think I have a good grasp on the particulars of the deal you're suggesting."
336.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_OrElse"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_OtherCustomers"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_Amount"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_RumburgGas_Logistics"] == true

338.speaker: Player_Romus
338.text: "I just don't see it. Even if my goal was to put the squeeze on Wehlen, this is not the most efficient way."

340.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
340.text: "Are you sure you don't want to hear my proposal, by the way?"

341.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
341.text: "Now, are you sure you don't want to hear my proposal regarding Wehlen?"

342.speaker: Player_Romus
342.text: "You do seem quite keen on it. I would be remiss not to hear you out."

345.speaker: Player_Romus
345.text: "Vina's a modest girl. She won't do anything worth gossiping about."

346.speaker: Player_Romus
346.text: "Good point. I'll start thinking about candidates."

347.speaker: Player_Romus
347.text: "Remind me, who is your son betrothed to again?"

348.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
348.text: "Why, the Duchess of Thompsfort, of course. Her family controls most of northwestern Rumburg. And she's got good birthing hips."

350.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
350.text: "Never underestimate the ability of the international press to manufacture royal scandals from thin air."

354.speaker: Player_Romus
354.text: "If the Rizian tabloids try something like that, I'll shut them down."

355.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
355.text: "It's not only Rizia who's paying attention, Your Majesty."

356.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
356.text: "Don't forget the rest of GRACE is invested in the Toras line of succession as well."

357.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
357.text: "As you can see, I put some careful thought into the decision. And so should you."

359.speaker: Player_Romus
359.text: "My daughter doesn't want my guidance anymore."

361.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
361.text: "But she may need it. Especially when it comes to her marriage."

364.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
364.text: "And don't forget that the rest of GRACE is invested in the Toras line of succession as well."

371.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
371.text: "Our partners will be looking for reassurance after your coronation speech."

376.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
376.text: "Just as the world's remaining monarchies pledge to enter an era of increased cooperation, you tell your entire country you intend on 'giving the people a voice'.

377.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
377.text: "What am I to make of that, Your Majesty? Or Nahrburk, or the Baronies of Soradis?"

378.speaker: Player_Romus
378.text: "Giving people a voice doesn't mean giving up monarchy. Isn't your own country governed by a parliament?"

379.speaker: Player_Romus
379.text: "I got carried away in the moment. I didn't really mean it."

380.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
380.text: "Technically, yes. But it has roughly as much power as your 'House of Delegates'."

381.speaker: Player_Romus
381.text: "You can all make of it what you will."

382.speaker: Player_Romus
382.text: "I didn't realize that GRACE was so attuned to my actions as king."

383.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
383.text: "You are the unproven ruler of one of GRACE's linchpin countries. Don't be surprised that you are under scrutiny."

387.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
387.text: "I hear your behavior as king has suggested otherwise."

388.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
388.text: "It's an odd promise to simply blurt out."

389.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
389.text: "I hardly think such a flippant answer is appropriate."

390.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
390.text: "You were lucky to escape the 1926 uprising with your head. To make such a public overture towards democracy is to tempt fate."

391.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
391.text: "Of course you are free to run your country the way you like. But without GRACE's backing, you will be at the mercy of ATO and the CSP like every other country on this continent."

392.speaker: Player_Romus
392.text: "Don't worry, Your Excellency. The Rizian monarchy is not going anywhere."

393.speaker: Player_Romus
393.text: "I know what I'm getting myself into."

394.speaker: Player_Romus
394.text: "Thank you for warning me. I shall keep your words in mind."

397.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
397.text: "I hope you shall do more than that."

404.speaker: Narrator
404.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn03_Beatrice_GRACEDiscussed"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Rumburg_HighEnergyExport"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Rumburg_AverageEnergyExport"] == true) == false)

407.speaker: Narrator
407.text: She folded her hands in her lap.

410.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
410.text: "I shall see you at supper, Your Majesty."

414.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
414.text: "Congratulations on your recent trade deal, by the way. Although I wouldn't trust the Sords any further than I could throw them."

416.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
416.text: "Rizia is one of its linchpin nations, after all."

418.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
418.text: "Do not discount the importance of our economic pact, Your Majesty."

419.speaker: Player_Romus
419.text: "I didn't realize our fellow kingdoms were keeping such a close eye on me."

420.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
420.text: "You are the unproven ruler of a country that possesses fabulous wealth. Don't be surprised you're under scrutiny."

421.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
421.text: "Our fellow monarchies want to see a stable Rizia. Especially after the summit at which we all promised closer cooperation."

422.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
422.text: "GRACE wants to see a stable Rizia. Especially after the summit at which we all promised closer cooperation."

423.speaker: Player_Romus
423.text: "I'll keep that in mind. We monarchies have to stick together."

424.speaker: Player_Romus
424.text: "I'm still not sure of the utility of such an organization."

425.speaker: Player_Romus
425.text: "Believe me, I want to see a stable Rizia as well."

430.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
430.text: "Together, we will ensure your lasting legacy."

431.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
431.text: "In case you haven't noticed, it's quite dangerous to be a monarch nowadays."

432.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
432.text: "Rumburg will do its best to aid you."

434.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
434.text: "There is safety in numbers. Even for those of us with well-equipped militaries."

436.speaker: Narrator
436.text: She walked out with her gown trailing behind her.

437.speaker: Narrator
437.text: The Queen gave the door a swift knock. Her attendants opened it, bowing as they did so.

458.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
458.text: "I feel obliged to ask once more: Are you positive you'll be able to deliver on Rizia's end of the bargain?"

459.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
459.text: "We'd then give you a one-year grace period to make the transition. After which, I warn you, our needs will be quite substantial."

460.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
460.text: "This will all need to be formalized by my parliament and your government, of course. A verbal agreement between in-laws is hardly sufficient."

461.speaker: Player_Romus
461.text: "I agree completely. My councilors and your foreign ministers can iron out the small print."

462.speaker: Player_Romus
462.text: "How long have we known each other, sweet Beatrice? My word is as good as gold."

463.speaker: Player_Romus
463.text: "It is still quite the leap of faith, though, isn't it? Is your sisterly affection for me that strong?"

464.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
464.text: "Precisely. We handle the big picture while the underlings take care of the particularities."

465.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
465.text: "I believe your intentions are nothing but pure, dear Romus. But we are a vast nation with freezing winters. I cannot stake my people's fate on an informal agreement."

466.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
466.text: "Our mutual love for Lena has indeed bound us tightly. But I confess we are also facing pressure to shift our energy purchases away from CSP and CSP-aligned countries."

467.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
467.text: "And given our numerous existing trade agreements, Rizia makes sense as a replacement."

468.speaker: Player_Romus
468.text: "With whom do you think you're speaking? King Romus always keeps a promise." [-3 Energy, -2 Energy Per Turn, +2 Budget Per Turn]

469.speaker: Player_Romus
469.text: "Well... you do have quite a large country. Perhaps you should halve your orders instead." [-2 Energy, -1 Energy Per Turn, +1 Budget Per Turn]

470.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
470.text: "Certainly, Your Majesty. It's important to be realistic about these matters."

472.speaker: Player_Romus
472.text: "If the Queen of Rumburg demands it, so it shall be." [-3 Energy, -2 Energy Per Turn, +2 Budget Per Turn]

474.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
474.text: "Certainly. It may not have as much of an impact as you were hoping, but it also won't be as much of a leap of faith on our part."

481.speaker: Narrator
481.text: My mother feigned a puzzled look.

482.speaker: Player_Romus
482.text: "I hope you had nothing to do with it."

505.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
505.text: "I have been notified of your expansion of the Monqiz port and dockyard facilities. This will easily handle the excess shipping traffic."

506.speaker: Player_Romus
506.text: "Indeed. I ordered that expansion with foreign trade in mind."

507.speaker: Player_Romus
507.text: "It's almost as if I knew this deal was coming. Just call me Romus the Prescient."

508.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
508.text: "I'd rather not. But I appreciate your forward thinking."

509.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
509.text: "Even if you don't agree to sell us gas, our gold trade will be much more efficient. Well done."

511.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
511.text: "Remember who got you into GRACE, Your Majesty. And on whose grace Rizia's trade depends."

512.speaker: Player_Romus
512.text: "Yes, I'm sure. Shall we change the subject?"

514.speaker: Player_Romus
514.text: "I remember just fine. Shall we change the subject?"

515.speaker: Player_Romus
515.text: "On second thought, this embargo could be quite useful. Let's go through with it."

519.speaker: Player_Romus
519.text: "I treasure our alliance, Beatrice. I just don't believe this deal is in Rizia's best interests."

521.speaker: Player_Romus
521.text: "Actually, I'm beginning to have second thoughts. Let's keep our trade relationship as it is."

522.speaker: Narrator
522.text: She gave me a disappointed frown.

523.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
523.text: "How cruel of you to get my hopes up like that."

525.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
525.text: "We Rumburgians do agree with Wehlen on one thing. The right of Dastnurists to practice their religion."

529.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
529.text: "So I was quite pleased to hear you granted the Dastnurists of Sallabes their long-overdue sanctuary expansion."

530.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
530.text: "I know Dastnurity is a minority religion over here. But it would be ever so kind of you to accommodate the community's needs."

531.speaker: Player_Romus
531.text: "Be honest with me. Do you really care about religion that much?"

532.speaker: Player_Romus
532.text: "I will try. But it's not at the top of my list of priorities."

533.speaker: Player_Romus
533.text: "Of course. The Kingdom of Rizia welcomes all denominations of Nurity."

534.speaker: Player_Romus
534.text: "Why should I accept them when they don't accept the sacred scripture of St. Wruhec?"

535.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
535.text: "For heaven's sake, Romus. Golcondists are hardly Wruhecists, and you accept them."

539.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
539.text: "Yes, you proved that, didn't you? An interesting decision, revoking your blasphemy law. One that will surely get Wehlen's attention..."

540.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
540.text: "Except Golcondists, it seems. One could only imagine Wehlen's wrath if you began tolerating them..."

544.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
544.text: "That's no attitude to take towards a small but significant part of your population."

545.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
545.text: "Keep your kingdom's faithful happy, and they will be your strongest supporters. Your so-called Wiseman should have told you that."

546.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
546.text: "Our personal beliefs don't factor into this, Romus."

547.speaker: Player_Romus
547.text: "It was the least I could do. I still regret that Lena was forced to convert."

548.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
548.text: "Past is past. I don't believe she ever truly accepted St. Wruhec's writings."

552.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
552.text: "She forgave you. Though I don't believe she ever truly accepted St. Wruhec's writings."

555.speaker: Beatrice Livingston (R)
555.text: "I suggest you rearrange that list, then."
